limitations: Low/central/high are explicit visualization scenarios, not censuses or statistical confidence intervals. Source headcounts remain unknown. Campaign tallies, surviving migrants, households, genetic ancestry and resident populations are distinct counting units. Component allocations and survival factors are model choices.

The animation is a focused Ramesside story, with per-model end dates after initial settlement. The full1400–900BCE scope remains in original evidence and sourceEvidenceWindow. Earlier dated presence is not retimed as an exact1300 arrival. Western source reservoirs are illustrative regional priors already present at the opening, not dated censuses or identical individuals living a century.

Traditional western/Aegean origins are the default: Sardinia for Sherden, Sicily for Shekelesh, Tyrrhenian Italy for Teresh, Crete for external Tjeker. Exact origin identifications remain contested. No universal Perire-survivor trip to Ugarit and back is compiled.

All nine group register rows and the entire supplied prose are retained. The evidence scope ends900BCE; later presence and identity records do not force the focused animation to keep running after settlement.

Western/eastern labels describe competing origin reconstructions, not resolved homelands or a compulsory reverse dispersal. Weshesh starts at an explicitly reconstructed Amurru proxy; Troy is not asserted.

Every geographic corridor, precise display year, release profile and regional population allocation is reconstructed. Contemporary documentary claims, later presence and identity formation remain distinct in the register.

Same-cohort links conserve a migration-history population between stages. Across generations they are accounting relationships, not proof of identical individuals; zero growth is a conservative closed-cohort display convention, not an estimate of historical fertility.

Perire losses are explicit scenario reductions of1000/3000/4000 people after arrivals, leaving500/1500/5000 survivors. These scenario losses are not a claim that the source tally was exact. No dead are transported as living settlers.

The local Dor scenario assigns two-thirds of the Tjeker-related display allocation to local coastal continuity and one-third to Cypriot integration. This is an illustrative regional model, not a measured local/foreign split. Its foreign entrant scope differs from the external hypothesis even though total displayed cohort volume is held fixed for comparison.
Northern Palistin/Walistin and Hiyawa political identities do not establish an ethnic population census. The north/south Peleset allocations visualize hypotheses without equating their residents.
Genetic ancestry percentages never determine population counts, dot sizes or ethnic colors. No continuously interpolated genetic halo or DNA map is invented from sparse samples.
The report supplies aggregate destruction-audit counts but no complete153-site event register; no invented destruction markers or blanket1200BCE fire horizon are generated.

Source approximate cumulative8800/25500/60000 is not adopted as a ledger total: low stage values already sum9000, and early/settled envelopes overlap. The review reports actual net entries and modeled losses separately.

Origins and resident stages use irregular reconstructed resource footprints: coastal plains, river terraces, cultivated basin margins and foothill corridors, land-clipped with modern Natural Earth. Polygon boundaries and within-footprint density are display assumptions; ancient shorelines, wetlands and channels have not been independently surveyed. Offshore guide nodes are navigation controls, not resident footprints.

Primary-source spot checks corroborate the limited Ashkelon sample finding and Dor architectural/pottery continuity. The synthesis, exact chronology options and all demographic envelopes are not independently verified in full.
